subject: SparkBridge grant: packaging exception & promotional credit request
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@sparkbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood credits & packaging for SparkBridge cohort

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiling and the per-route cost visibility. SparkBridge is finalizing benefits for our next cohort (September intake) and we want to include a Redwood promotional pack for 12 startups.

Quick summary of ask:
- 12 startups, each gets $6k in free credits to run pilot workloads for 3 months
- One shared sandbox project for the cohort with read-only observability for SparkBridge staff
- A 20% promotional discount on committed blocks if any startup converts within 6 months

We have some internal flexibility on how credits are issued (per-company vs pooled) — attaching the program brief for context. Can Redwood do an exception to standard promo caps and sign a short-term addendum? Also, if reserved capacity or a sponsor package makes sense, happy to discuss.

Attachment: SparkBridge_Startup_Pack.pdf

Appreciate any ballpark numbers and whether this needs legal signoff or a special approval.

Thanks,
Emily Chen
Program Director, SparkBridge Labs
emily.chen@sparkbridge.com
+1 (415) 555-0124
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@sparkbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood credits & packaging for SparkBridge cohort

Hi Emily — really appreciate the clear asks and the brief. Nice to see cohort sizing.

High-level response (ballpark):
- Credits: We can do $6k equivalent per company for 12 companies (total $72k) as a promotional grant tied to the cohort, with usage reporting for each company.
- Sandbox: We can create a shared sandbox project and grant SparkBridge read-only access; we'll need a small MSA addendum to document data access and retention for the shared view.
- Conversion discount: 15% standard promotional discount is doable without exec signoff; 20% is above our typical cap and will need a one-time approval from Revenue Ops.

Practical next steps from our side:
1) Internal approval for the 20% promotional discount (if you need 20%).
2) Decide whether credits are issued to each company or pooled (we prefer per-company for observability).
3) Term sheet redline (I'll propose language for the addendum and send it internally for signoff).

I'm looping in Monica (billing/packaging) and Vanessa (Head of GTM programs) to confirm operational feasibility and who can approve a >15% promo.

Would you be available for a 30-min call on Wednesday to lock the details?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: SparkBridge credits request — approval needed for 20% promo

Vanessa / Monica,

Forwarding SparkBridge's ask. Key points: $72k total credits (12 x $6k), shared sandbox with read-only access, and they want a 20% conversion discount for any startup that buys within 6 months.

Questions for you:
- Vanessa: do we have a precedent for cohort-wide grants issued per-company vs pooled? Any program playbook we should follow?
- Monica: pricing — we can offer 15% marketing promo without additional approval. 20% requires a pricing exception; is there a simple approval path (VP sign-off or Revenue Ops ticket)?

I'm attaching a quick redline to the standard partner addendum that captures the sandbox access and credit tracking fields. This is intentionally light — want Ops to approve before I send back to them.

Attachment: term-sheet-redline.docx

If you want any edits, I can update and get back to Emily tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SparkBridge credits request — approval needed for 20% promo

Marcus / Monica — thanks for the clear summary. A few operational notes: 

- Precedent: We have issued cohort grants as per-company credits (makes reporting and future conversions cleaner).
- Sandbox access: legal will want the addendum; keep it scoped to read-only metrics and no data egress. Term: 90 days for the cohort pilot.
- Pricing exception: I can approve a one-time 20% promo for partner-led cohorts if total committed ARR upside (modeled) exceeds 3x the grant value within 12 months. For SparkBridge, if even 2-3 conversions at our Starter or Growth tier look likely, this passes the bar.

Ask from me: Marcus, can you include a short conversion estimate in the note back to Emily (e.g., expected conversion range and which tiers we think are appropriate)? That helps me document the rationale when I sign.

I'll sign the pricing exception form once you include the conversion expectation and confirm the sandbox scope.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of GTM Programs, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@sparkbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood credits & packaging for SparkBridge cohort — proposal attached

Hi Emily — quick update and next steps.

Thanks — Vanessa has agreed to a one-time 20% conversion promo conditional on expected conversion economics (her note below). Our recommended packaging:
- Credits: $6k allocated to each of 12 startups (total $72k). Issued per-company; credits expire 90 days after activation.
- Sandbox: single cohort project with read-only dashboard access for SparkBridge staff (no data export). 90-day access window tied to the cohort.
- Conversion discount: 20% off listing price for any startup that signs a committed block within 6 months; Redwood requires at least 2 expected conversions at Starter/Growth to approve.

Conversion estimate (conservative): 2–4 startups signing Starter (avg first-year committed spend ~ $12k), upside scenario 4–6 signing across Starter/Growth. If 2 convert at Starter, expected committed ARR > 3x grant value (meets Vanessa's criteria).

I've attached a light partner addendum redline and a polished proposal for you to share with the cohort. If that looks good, I'll route a pricing exception form internally (Vanessa will sign) and then send the DocuSign for your signature.

Attachments: proposal-v2.pdf, term-sheet-redline.docx
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/XYZ-998877

Would you like a 30-min sync Friday to finalize prior to cohort kickoff?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
